##Pulling Data & Imagery


```{r ALL data pull, message = FALSE}
#Grabbing Sample ID's
soil_points <- st_read("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/fixed_soil_points2.shp") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("CID","SPID"), names_to ="type", values_to = "ID")
  

#CSV of AESL data:
soil_all <- read.csv("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/Perry_all_samples_all(in).csv")

# Merge points + sample data:
soil_points <- merge(soil_points, soil_all, by = "ID") #CID and SPID


write_csv(soil_points, "../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/soil_points.csv")

# Load the USGS 1m DEM (acts as the template)
USGS_DEM <- rast("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/DEM rasters/output_USGS1m.tif")

# border:
border <- vect("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/Border/border_17N.shp") #points 124 and 136 are NOT within bounds. That's why we are using different border
border_ext <-ext(border)

#topo stack:
clipped_stack <- terra::rast("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/clipped_stack.tif") 

#surface reflectance run through PCA:
PCA_SR <- terra::rast("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/PCA_SR.tif") 

#NDVI:
NDVI <- terra::rast("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/NDVI.tif") 

```





```{r wrangling}


#stack all
covariates <- c(PCA_SR, clipped_stack, NDVI)

#make names valid
names(covariates) <- make.names(names(covariates))

#sort by SINGLE POINT DATA
soil_points_singlepoint <- filter(soil_points, type == "SPID")

#sort by COMPOSITE DATA
soil_points_composite <- filter(soil_points, type == "CID")

# vect the sample data
soil_points_vect_SP <- vect(soil_points_singlepoint)
soil_points_vect_C <- vect(soil_points_composite)


# Extract raster values at soil sample points
soil_points_SPID <- terra::extract(covariates, soil_points_vect_SP, bind = T,xy = T)
soil_points_CID <- terra::extract(covariates, soil_points_vect_C, bind = T,xy = T)


#convert to df
soils_df_SP <- as.data.frame(soil_points_SPID)
soils_df_C <- as.data.frame(soil_points_CID)

# Select only the soil property columns
soil_df_cols_SP <- soils_df_SP[, c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'P', 'Zn')]
soil_df_cols_C <- soils_df_C[, c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'P', 'Zn')]


#exclude non essential data:
soils_df_wrang_SP <- soils_df_SP[ ,-(1:9)]
soils_df_wrang_C <- soils_df_C[ ,-(1:9)]

```

```{r Composite vs. Single point plots}
soil_nutrients <- c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'P', 'Zn')

# Make sure data frames have the same number of rows
stopifnot(nrow(soils_df_SP) == nrow(soils_df_C))

# Build data for plotting
plot_df <- map_dfr(soil_nutrients, function(nutrient) {
  tibble(
    Nutrient = nutrient,
    Composite = soils_df_C[[nutrient]],
    SinglePoint = soils_df_SP[[nutrient]]
  )
})

# Compute per-nutrient Pearson correlation
corr_df <- plot_df %>%
  group_by(Nutrient) %>%
  summarize(
    cor = cor(Composite, SinglePoint, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  )

# Plot with 1:1 line and correlation annotation
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Composite, y = SinglePoint)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "forestgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~Nutrient, scales = "free") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(
    data = corr_df,
    aes(
      x = -Inf, y = Inf,
      label = paste0("r = ", round(cor, 2))
    ),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 4, color = "navy", inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Composite vs Single Point Soil Nutrient Values",
    x = "Composite Value",
    y = "Single Point Value"
  )
```
```{r C vs SP without outliers}
soil_nutrients <- c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'P', 'Zn')

# Remove outliers (optional; comment this section if not needed)
plot_df <- map_dfr(soil_nutrients, function(nutrient) {
  df <- tibble(
    Nutrient = nutrient,
    Composite = soils_df_C[[nutrient]],
    SinglePoint = soils_df_SP[[nutrient]]
  )
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(Composite), !is.na(SinglePoint))
  c_mean <- mean(df$Composite)
  c_sd <- sd(df$Composite)
  s_mean <- mean(df$SinglePoint)
  s_sd <- sd(df$SinglePoint)
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      abs(Composite - c_mean) <= 3 * c_sd,
      abs(SinglePoint - s_mean) <= 3 * s_sd
    )
  return(df)
})

# Calculate r and p-value per nutrient
stat_df <- plot_df %>%
  group_by(Nutrient) %>%
  summarize(
    r = cor(Composite, SinglePoint, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
    p = cor.test(Composite, SinglePoint)$p.value
  )

# Plot with r and p-value on each facet
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Composite, y = SinglePoint)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "forestgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~Nutrient, scales = "free") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(
    data = stat_df,
    aes(
      x = -Inf, y = Inf,
      label = paste0("r = ", round(r, 2), "\np = ", signif(p, 2))
    ),
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 4, color = "navy", inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Composite vs Single Point Soil Nutrient Values",
    x = "Composite Value",
    y = "Single Point Value"
  )
```



##RF
###Correlation Matrix
```{r CM }
# Compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix_SP <- cor(soils_df_wrang_SP, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
cor_matrix_C <- cor(soils_df_wrang_C, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

```

```{r plotting CM }
#formatting:
ggcorrplot(cor_matrix_SP, type = "lower", 
           lab = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE, 
           tl.cex = 4, # Adjust text size
           lab_size = 2, # Adjust correlation label size
           tl.srt = 45) # Rotate axis labels

ggcorrplot(cor_matrix_SP, type = "lower",
           lab = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE,
           tl.cex = 4, # Adjust text size
           lab_size = 2, # Adjust correlation label size
           tl.srt = 45,
           hc.order = TRUE, # Cluster similar variables together
           insig = "blank", # Hide insignificant correlations
           p.mat = cor_pmat(soils_df_wrang_SP)
           ) # Rotate axis labels


# col name of soil properties
soil_vars <- colnames(soil_df_cols_SP)
# topo name list
topo_vars <- setdiff(colnames(soils_df_wrang_SP), soil_vars)

# Compute correlation matrix only between soil properties and topo rasters
cor_matrix_soil_topo_SP <- cor(soils_df_wrang_SP[, soil_vars], soils_df_wrang_SP[, topo_vars], 
                            use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# Visualize
ggcorrplot(cor_matrix_soil_topo_SP, lab = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE, 
           tl.cex = 5, lab_size = 2, tl.srt = 45, method = "circle")

#save png of corr matrix
#ggsave("../Mapping/Output/Correlation_Matrix_all.png")


# Define the variables to exclude from the y-axis (e.g., nutrients and coordinates)
variables_to_exclude <- c("Ca", "K", "Mg", "Mn", "Zn", "LBC.1", "LBCeq", "pH.2", "x", "y", "P")

# Step 1: Keep only the `P` column from the correlation matrix
cor_matrix_filtered <- cor_matrix_SP[, "P", drop = FALSE]  # Keep only the column for P

# Step 2: Exclude rows corresponding to the variables to exclude (including "P")
cor_matrix_filtered <- cor_matrix_filtered[!rownames(cor_matrix_filtered) %in% variables_to_exclude, , drop = FALSE]

# Step 3: Filter out uncorrelated variables based on a threshold (optional)
correlation_threshold <- 0.15  # Define threshold for minimum correlation
cor_matrix_filtered <- cor_matrix_filtered[abs(cor_matrix_filtered) > correlation_threshold, , drop = FALSE]

# Step 4: Sort correlations by absolute value for better visualization (optional)
cor_matrix_sorted <- cor_matrix_filtered[order(abs(cor_matrix_filtered), decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]

# Step 5: Create a vertical correlation plot with `P` on the x-axis only
ggcorrplot(as.matrix(cor_matrix_sorted), type = "full",
           lab = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE,
           tl.cex = 8, # Adjust text size
           lab_size = 2, # Adjust correlation label size
           tl.srt = 45) # Rotate axis labels


# Optional: Save the plot as a PNG
ggsave("../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/output/P_corrplot.png", dpi = 300, 
       width = 8, height = 6, units = "in")
```

```{r whole P process}
#stratify P split:
set.seed(623)
  set_P_split <- initial_split(soils_df_wrang_SP,prop = 0.8, strata = P) 
  
  set_P_train <- training(set_P_split) %>%
    select(c(P,Comp.1:NDVI)) %>%
    na.omit()
  
  set_P_test <- testing(set_P_split) %>%
    select(c(P,Comp.1:NDVI)) %>%
    na.omit()
  
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = set_P_train,

#RF:

  dplyr::select(-c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'Zn','x','y'))

  # Create the trainControl object
  control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10) # Example: 10-fold cross-validation
  
  # Use the train function
  set_df_P_strata <- train(P ~ ., 
                           data = set_P_train, 
                           method = "rf",

#McNears new:
# Step 1: Manually sum diagonal (correct) and off-diagonal (incorrect) elements
rf_correct <- sum(c(23, 0, 0, 0))  # Diagonal elements for RF
rf_incorrect <- sum(c(3, 2, 0, 0))  # Off-diagonal elements for RF

krige_correct <- sum(c(25, 0, 0, 0))  # Diagonal elements for Kriged
krige_incorrect <- sum(c(3, 0, 0, 0))  # Off-diagonal elements for Kriged

# Step 2: Create a 2x2 contingency table
contingency_table <- matrix(c(rf_correct, rf_incorrect, krige_correct, krige_incorrect),
                            nrow = 2,
                            byrow = TRUE,
                            dimnames = list(
                              Classifier = c("RF", "Kriged"),
                              Outcome = c("Correct", "Incorrect")
                            ))

print("Contingency Table:")
print(contingency_table)

# Step 3: Perform McNemar's Test
mcnemar_result <- mcnemar.test(contingency_table)

# Display the results
print("McNemar's Test Results:")
print(mcnemar_result)

            # n_01: Kriged is correct, but RF is incorrect

            # n_11: Both models agree and are correct

            # n_00: Both models are incorrect
```

```{r}
# Constants
P_CLASS_MATRIX <- matrix(
  c(0, 30, 1, 30, 60, 2, 60, 100, 3, 100, Inf, 4),
  ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

P_PERSCRIPTIONS <- c(
  "Apply 140 lbs of P205 per acre",
  "Apply 105 lbs of P205 per acre",
  "Apply 75 lbs of P205 per acre",
  "Apply 0 lbs of P205 per acre"
)
CUSTOM_COLORS <- c("#88CCEE", "#44AA99", "#DDCC77", "#CC6677")

# Convert P from ppm to lbs/acre
convert_ppm_to_lbs_per_acre <- function(ppm) {
  ppm * 2  # Conversion factor
}

# Helper function: Reclassify raster
reclassify_p <- function(raster, class_matrix, labels) {
  classified <- classify(raster, class_matrix)
  levels(classified) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = labels)
  return(classified)
}

# 1. Data Preparation
set.seed(623)
soils_df_wrang_SP$P <- convert_ppm_to_lbs_per_acre(soils_df_wrang_SP$P)  # Convert P to lbs/acre
set_P_split <- initial_split(soils_df_wrang_SP, prop = 0.8, strata = P)
set_P_train <- training(set_P_split)
set_P_test <- testing(set_P_split)

# Plot training and testing densities
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = set_P_train, aes(x = P), color = "red") +
  geom_density(data = set_P_test, aes(x = P), color = "blue") +
  ggtitle("Density of Training and Testing Sets")

# 2. Random Forest Model
set_P_strata <- set_P_train %>%
  dplyr::select(-c('LBC.1', 'LBCeq', 'pH.2', 'Ca', 'K', 'Mg', 'Mn', 'Zn', 'x', 'y'))
rf_model <- train(P ~ ., data = set_P_strata, method = "rf", trControl = trainControl)
P_predicted_rf <- terra::predict(covariates, rf_model, na.rm = TRUE)

# Reintroduce points
soil_points_sf <- st_as_sf(set_P_train, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(covariates))
coords <- st_coordinates(soil_points_sf)
P_predicted_rf[terra::cellFromXY(P_predicted_rf, coords)] <- soil_points_sf$P
#mask
P_predicted_rf_mask <- terra::mask(P_predicted_rf, border)

# Classify RF predictions
P_rf_classified <- reclassify_p(P_predicted_rf, P_CLASS_MATRIX, P_PERSCRIPTIONS)

# 3. Kriging
# coordinates(set_P_train) <- data.frame(x = set_P_train$x, y = set_P_train$y)
proj4string(set_P_train) <- CRS("+proj=utm +zone=17 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs")
set_P_train <- spTransform(set_P_train, CRS(proj4string(grid_sp)))
variogram_model <- fit.variogram(variogram(P ~ 1, set_P_train), vgm("Sph"))
kriged_raster <- Krig(P ~ 1, set_P_train, "Sph")

# Classify Kriged predictions
P_krig_classified <- reclassify_p(kriged_raster, P_CLASS_MATRIX, P_PERSCRIPTIONS)
P_krig_classified_mask <- terra::mask(P_krig_classified, border)
# 4. Aggregation and Sieving
P_rf_aggregated <- terra::aggregate(P_rf_classified, fact = 10, fun = modal, expand = TRUE)
P_rf_sieved <- terra::sieve(P_rf_aggregated, threshold = 40)

# Update levels for sieved raster
levels(P_rf_sieved) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = P_PERSCRIPTIONS)
#mask:
P_rf_sieved <- terra::mask(P_rf_sieved, border)
# Save results
writeRaster(P_rf_sieved, "../Local Data- DO NOT PUSH/P_rf_sieved.tif", overwrite = TRUE)

# 5. Confusion Matrix
        set_P_test <- set_P_test %>%
          mutate(
            true_category = case_when(
              P <= 30 ~ P_PERSCRIPTIONS[1],
              P <= 60 ~ P_PERSCRIPTIONS[2],
              P <= 100 ~ P_PERSCRIPTIONS[3],
              P > 100 ~ P_PERSCRIPTIONS[4]
            )
          )
        
        # RF Confusion Matrix
        set_P_test$rf_predicted <- terra::extract(P_rf_sieved, set_P_test[, c("x", "y")])[, 2]
        confusion_rf <- confusionMatrix(
          factor(set_P_test$rf_predicted, levels = P_PERSCRIPTIONS),
          factor(set_P_test$true_category, levels = P_PERSCRIPTIONS)
        )
        
        # Kriging Confusion Matrix
        set_P_test$kriged_predicted <- terra::extract(P_krig_classified, set_P_test[, c("x", "y")])[, 2]
        confusion_kriging <- confusionMatrix(
          factor(set_P_test$kriged_predicted, levels = P_PERSCRIPTIONS),
          factor(set_P_test$true_category, levels = P_PERSCRIPTIONS)
        )
        # Extract predictions and true categories
        rf_predictions <- set_P_test$rf_predicted
        kriging_predictions <- set_P_test$kriged_predicted
        true_categories <- set_P_test$true_category
        
        # Create a contingency table for McNemar's test
        mcnemar_table <- table(
          RF = rf_predictions == true_categories,    # RF correctness (TRUE/FALSE)
          Kriging = kriging_predictions == true_categories # Kriging correctness (TRUE/FALSE)
        )

# Perform McNemar's test
mcnemar_result <- mcnemar.test(mcnemar_table)

# Print results
print("Contingency Table for McNemar's Test:")
print(mcnemar_table)

print("McNemar's Test Results:")
print(mcnemar_result)

# 6. Plotting
```

#Kriging:
```{r krig setup}

#setting grid as points for kriging
grid<-as.points(covariates)

  #plot(grid)
#set to sf format
grid_sf <- st_as_sf(grid)

grid_sp <- as_Spatial(grid_sf)

soil_points_sf_CID <- st_as_sf(soil_points_CID)

soil_points_sp_CID <- as_Spatial(soil_points_sf_CID)

#variograms:
VarioC <- function(nutrient,data, vgm) {
nut_var<-variogram(nutrient,data = data) 
nut_varfit <- fit.variogram(nut_var, model = vgm(vgm)) 
plot(nut_var, nut_varfit, main = nutrient, sub = "Composite")}

VarioSP <- function(nutrient,data, vgm) {
nut_var<-variogram(nutrient,data = data) 
nut_varfit <- fit.variogram(nut_var, model = vgm(vgm)) 
plot(nut_var, nut_varfit, main = nutrient, sub = "Single Point")}

# Variogram and Kriging Function
Krig <- function(nutrient, data, vgm_model) {
  # Variogram
  nut_var <- variogram(nutrient, data = data)
  nut_varfit <- fit.variogram(nut_var, model = vgm(vgm_model))
  plot(nut_var, nut_varfit, main = nutrient, sub = "Kriging Variogram")
  
  # Kriging
  nut_kriged <- krige(nutrient, data, grid_sp, model = nut_varfit) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    vect()
  
  # Convert to raster
  nut_kriged_raster <- rasterize(nut_kriged, covariates, field = "var1.pred")
  return(nut_kriged_raster)
}

```

```{r classify P}

#clip:

P_rf_clip_strata <- terra::mask(P_predict_strata, border)
P_krig_clip_strata <- terra::mask(P_krig_SP, border)

#"Low P (0-30 lbs/A)" Apply 140 lbs of P205 per acre
#"Medium P (31-60 lbs/A)" Apply 105 lbs of P205 per acre
#"High P (61-100 lbs/A)" Apply 75 lbs of P205 per acre
#"Very High P (100+ lbs/A)" Apply 0 lbs of P205 per acre



# Define breaks and corresponding labels for Phosphorus (in ppm)
P_classes <- c(0, 30, 50, Inf)  # Breakpoints
P_labels <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)  # Assign numeric labels

# Create classification matrices
P_class_matrix <- cbind(P_classes[-length(P_classes)], P_classes[-1], P_labels)



# Classify P rasters
P_predict_classified <- classify(P_rf_clip_strata, P_class_matrix)
P_kriged_classified <- classify(P_krig_clip_strata, P_class_matrix)


# Assign category labels
P_labels_factor <- c("Apply 140 lbs of P205 per acre", 
          "Apply 105 lbs of P205 per acre",
          "Apply 75 lbs of P205 per acre", 
          "Apply 0 lbs of P205 per acre")


# Convert rasters to categorical factors
levels(P_predict_classified) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = P_labels_factor)
levels(P_kriged_classified) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = P_labels_factor)


par(mfrow = c(2,2))
  #adjusted P
  
  
  # Classify P rasters #P adjusted is just forcing the soil points in
  
P_predict_classified_adjust <- classify(P_predict_adjusted_SP, P_class_matrix)


# Assign category labels  for P:

# Convert rasters to categorical factors
levels(P_predict_classified) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = P_labels_factor)
levels(P_kriged_classified) <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, category = P_labels_factor)


par(mfrow = c(2,2))
#RF
plot(P_predict_classified, main = "Classified P (RF Prediction)")
#Kriging
plot(P_kriged_classified, main = "Classified P (Kriging)")

# Reclassify P values in P_test using the same class breaks
P_test$classified_P <- cut(
  P_test$P, 
  breaks = P_classes, 
  labels = P_labels_factor, 
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Convert the classified column to a factor with consistent levels
P_test$classified_P <- factor(P_test$classified_P, levels = P_labels_factor)


```

```{r P clustering}

library(igraph)
# 1. Aggregate (Optional: Only if you want to reduce resolution)
# Example: Aggregate by a factor of 2 (adjust as needed)
P_rf_agg <- terra::aggregate(P_predict_classified_adjust, fact= 2, fun=modal, expand=TRUE)

# 2. Clump: Identify connected regions with the same value
# P_rf_clumped <- raster::clump(raster::raster(P_rf_agg), directions=8)  # Uses 8-direction connectivity

# 3. Sieve: Remove small isolated clumps (e.g., smaller than 5 cells)
P_rf_sieved <- terra::sieve(P_rf_agg, threshold=2)


# 4. Plot to check the results
plot(P_rf_sieved, main="Cleaned RF Map (Aggregated, Clumped, and Sieved)")
writeRaster(P_rf_sieved, "P_rf_sieved.tif", overwrite=TRUE)
```

```{r}
P_test$predicted_category <- factor(P_test$predicted_category, levels = P_labels_factor)

correct_predictions <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix))  # Sum of diagonal elements
total_observations <- sum(confusion_matrix)         # Total number of observations

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy <- correct_predictions / total_observations

# Print accuracy
print(paste("Accuracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```

```{r Validate P Classification}
#Test P classification:                            
reclassify_P <- function(P) {
  if (is.na(P)) return(NA)  # Handle NA values
  if (P <= 30) return("Low P (0-30 lbs/A)")  # Low category
  else if (P <= 60) return("Medium P (31-60 lbs/A)")  # Medium category
  else if (P <= 100) return("High P (61-100 lbs/A)")  # High category
  else return("Very High P (>100 lbs/A)")  # Very High category
}
extracted_P_class <- terra::extract(P_predict_classified, P_test_sf, cells = TRUE)
#Classify:
P_test$reclassified_category <- sapply(P_test$P, reclassify_P)

# Compare with P_classified
comparison <- data.frame(
  P_test_ID = 1:nrow(P_test),
  P_test_category = P_test$reclassified_category,
  Extracted_category = extracted_P_class$category
)

# mismatches
mismatches <- comparison[comparison$P_test_category != comparison$Extracted_category, ]
cat("Number of mismatched classifications:", nrow(mismatches), "\n")

# confusion matrix
library(caret)
confusion <- confusionMatrix(
  factor(comparison$P_test_category, levels = unique(c(comparison$P_test_category, comparison$Extracted_category))),
  factor(comparison$Extracted_category, levels = unique(c(comparison$P_test_category, comparison$Extracted_category)))
)

# print cm
print("Confusion Matrix:")
print(confusion)


```

```{r Validation P rf sieved}
# Step 1: Extract values from the cleaned raster at test locations
P_test$cleaned_rf_value <- terra::extract(P_rf_sieved, P_test[, c("x", "y")])[, 2]  # Extract raster values


# Step 3: Reclassify the extracted raster values to match the categories
P_test$cleaned_rf_category <- sapply(P_test$cleaned_rf_value, reclassify_P)

# Step 4: Compare the cleaned raster categories with the true categories
comparison_cleaned_rf <- data.frame(
  True_Category = P_test$reclassified_category,  # True categories from P_test
  Cleaned_RF_Category = P_test$cleaned_rf_category  # Extracted and reclassified raster categories
)

# Step 5: Generate the confusion matrix
confusion_cleaned_rf <- confusionMatrix(
  factor(comparison_cleaned_rf$True_Category, levels = c("Low P (0-30 lbs/A)", 
                                                         "Medium P (31-60 lbs/A)", 
                                                         "High P (61-100 lbs/A)", 
                                                         "Very High P (>100 lbs/A)")),
  factor(comparison_cleaned_rf$Cleaned_RF_Category, levels = c("Low P (0-30 lbs/A)", 
                                                               "Medium P (31-60 lbs/A)", 
                                                               "High P (61-100 lbs/A)", 
                                                               "Very High P (>100 lbs/A)"))
)

# Step 6: Output the confusion matrix
print("Confusion Matrix for Cleaned RF Map:")
print(confusion_cleaned_rf)
```
